answer: Cluster co-activity fingerprinting flags Sybils by behavioral signature. Agents that repeatedly appear in the same transaction subgraphs within tight time windows form a haven for colluders, so detection scores pairwise co-occurrence against a chance baseline. Flagged clusters get throttled from the shared vault of unclaimed rewards, raising each fake identity's cost since attackers must dilute coordination across disjoint clusters. At scale this drives attacker profitability toward its nadir, forcing far more identities than payoff justifies.
